items.statement: For infants aged 8 weeks or older, the direct-cessation protocol will reduce the weekly median time on high flow from about 52 to 32 hours or less during the 2026 to 2027 season, with re-escalation within 24 hours staying at or below 12 percent.
items.rationale: Supported by a trial and a ward report (claims c1, c2); the age limit follows the unresolved conflict (claim c3).
items.risks: Missed night checks; a severe season could lengthen stays regardless.

items.statement: Night-time trials off will lag day-time trials off by more than four hours unless the protocol sets a fixed 22:00 assessment.
items.rationale: Night checks are often missed (claim c4).
items.risks: Adds a scheduled check at a busy time.

items.statement: Direct cessation is as safe in infants under 8 weeks as in older infants.
items.rationale: This is the contested question (claim c3), but one ward in one season will see too few young infants on high flow to answer it.
items.risks: Testing it here would expose the youngest infants to an unresolved risk.

summary: Three hypotheses; h1 selected with an age limit, h3 recorded and not pursued on this ward.
